subject: OrbitCloud procurement: SLO / metrics access questionnaire — clarifications
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura@orbitcloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitcloud.com
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Procurement questionnaire: SLO measurement + monitoring

Ben —

Thanks for agreeing to coordinate on OrbitCloud's procurement questionnaire. We're in the final stages of vendor review and need a short packet describing how Redwood measures and exposes SLOs (uptime and latency), how alerts are generated, and what customer access looks like. Our legal/procurement team has a few nonstandard asks around temporary exceptions for long‑term metric retention during the first 6 months of onboarding — see attached questionnaire (procurement-slo-questions.docx).

High level items we need answered:
- Definition of 'downtime' for hosted API vs dedicated/private deployments
- Which latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) you publish as SLOs and which you use for internal alerting
- How cold starts, autoscale-up events, and cache-warmup are handled in SLO calculations
- What parts of monitoring customers can see (dashboards, raw timeseries, aggregated SLO windows)
- Alerting thresholds and incident routing (email/SMS/Slack) for customers vs Redwood internal ops
- Evidence we can request for procurement (samples of uptime history, retention policy, export format)

Could you confirm who on your side will handle the technical answers and whether you can provide an evidence packet by next Tuesday?

Best,
Laura Chen
Head of Vendor Ops
OrbitCloud

Attachment: procurement-slo-questions.docx (docx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@orbitcloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: SLO measurement + monitoring

Laura —

Thanks for the clear list. Forwarding to our reliability and sales engineering leads (David + Marissa) to compile the technical packet. Quick summary upfront so your procurement team has the key answers while we assemble supporting evidence: 

- Downtime definition: For Redwood Hosted API, we define "service-unavailable" as HTTP 5xx or connection failures that affect customer‑facing inference requests; we exclude planned maintenance windows that were pre-notified. For Dedicated and Private, downtime definitions can be scoped in the contract (we typically map to capacity/endpoint health checks).
- Latency SLOs we publish: p95 for interactive latency commitments (default); p99 is used as an internal signal for tail degradation and for high-tier contracts.
- Cold starts & autoscale: We apply a configurable warmup exclusion window (default 30s–2m depending on model size) that is documented and optionally negotiable for Dedicated.
- Customer access: We provide a per-route dashboard (Grafana) with p50/p90/p95/p99 timeseries, request rates, and error trends; customers can request CSV export for a 90-day window by default.
- Alerts: Customers can subscribe to incident notifications via email and webhook; critical paging is handled by Redwood on Dedicated contracts with an on-call rotation.

We'll attach a short evidence checklist and a sample CSV export. David — can you add the precise measurement window math and the Grafana embed link?

I can deliver the evidence packet by next Tuesday EOD.

—Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Looping in a quick procurement note — OrbitCloud asked about a temporary exception for metric retention during the ramp (first 6 months). We typically allow a 30–90 day retention default for hosted plans and offer a retention add-on for longer windows. For procurement, we can propose a 6‑month trial of extended retention with an explicit evidence handoff at month 3 and month 6.

If OrbitCloud needs a formal carveout during onboarding (e.g., to satisfy a compliance review), we'll propose an SLA amendment with agreed export checkpoints and a dedicated SRE touchpoint for the first 60 days. David — please list what exports we can promise as checkpoints.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura@orbitcloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitcloud.com
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: SLO measurement + monitoring

Thanks — a few follow-ups from procurement. Can you clarify: 
1) Exactly which requests are excluded from SLO calculation (health-check pings, internal admin calls, orchestration probes)?
2) For latency SLOs, does Redwood compute percentiles on the raw per-request latency or on aggregated per-minute buckets?
3) If we request p99 history for the prior 12 months for an audit, what format/retention would you provide and what lead time is needed?

Also, procurement flagged the warmup window as subjective. We need a more deterministic rule they can include in the contract. Can you provide a deterministic warmup formula (for example: exclude first N requests after instance creation where N = max(20, 0.01 * expected_concurrency))?

Appreciate details — Laura

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@orbitcloud.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 14:35:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Procurement questionnaire: SLO measurement + monitoring

Laura —

Thanks for the sharp questions. Below are the specifics you can put into procurement language; I'm pasting the same content into the evidence packet and will attach a sample CSV (redwood-slo-metrics-sample.csv) and the evidence checklist.

1) Exclusions from SLO calculation
- Exclude synthetic health probes (any request with header X-Redwood-Probe: true)
- Exclude internal admin/api-token verification calls originating from Redwood management plane IPs
- Exclude telemetry/backfill jobs from batch exports

2) Percentile computation method
- We compute percentiles on a two-tier aggregation: raw per-request latencies are captured and stored briefly, then we roll them into 1-minute aggregated buckets. Published SLO percentiles (p50/p95/p99) are computed from the per-minute buckets across the measurement window (standard window = 30 days). This reduces sensitivity to per-request outliers but preserves tail characteristics. For audit exports we can provide per-minute buckets for up to 12 months (CSV).

3) 12-month p99 history and retention
- For Hosted plans: default retention for per-minute buckets is 90 days. For procurement/enterprise deals we can provide a 12-month export as part of a contract amendment; lead time typically 5 business days to generate and provide the CSV export. For Dedicated/Private we can negotiate longer retention or on-prem ingestion.

4) Deterministic warmup rule (recommended contract wording)
- Warmup exclusion applies for the first N inference requests processed by a newly provisioned instance where N = max(25, ceil(0.02 * expected_concurrency_per_instance)). For very large models this is capped at 500 requests. The instance creation timestamp will be recorded in our control plane and used to tag warmup-excluded requests. This formulation is deterministic and verifiable in logs.

5) Alerts and customer visibility
- Customers see per-route dashboards with p50/p90/p95/p99 charts, request rate, and error rate. They can create alert rules for thresholds on p95/p99 or error rate. Critical incident paging is available for enterprise contracts.

Evidence and next steps
- Attached: redwood-slo-evidence-checklist.pdf and redwood-slo-metrics-sample.csv (per-minute bucket sample).
- We can provide the 12-month p99 CSV export within 5 business days subject to an executed amendment.

Proposed next step: 30‑minute technical sync this week to confirm wording and timeline; I'm available Thu/Fri afternoons.

—David
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-slo-metrics-sample.csv (CSV)
